court: Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit

issues.label: Court jurisdiction and venue
issues.why: The court must confirm statutory jurisdiction and proper venue to review a TSCA §6(h) final rule.

issues.label: Final agency action
issues.why: The court must determine whether the 2024 Rule (and any aspects of the 2021 Rule still at issue) constitutes reviewable final agency action.

issues.label: Timeliness of petitions
issues.why: The court must ensure the petition for review of the 2024 Rule and the consolidated challenge are timely under TSCA’s judicial-review deadlines.

issues.label: Effect of voluntary remand
issues.why: The court must decide how the 2022 voluntary remand of the 2021 Rule affects remaining claims and what portions are moot or superseded.

issues.label: Mootness of 2021 claims
issues.why: The court must assess whether amendments in 2024 moot challenges to the 2021 Rule or leave live disputes.

issues.label: Scope of consolidation
issues.why: The court must define what issues are properly before it from the consolidated petitions and any limits on review.

issues.label: Standing of petitioners
issues.why: The court must confirm Article III standing (injury, causation, redressability) for each petitioner and claim.

issues.label: Organizational standing elements
issues.why: The court must evaluate member injury, germaneness, and participation requirements for associational standing.

issues.label: Ripeness of challenges
issues.why: The court must decide whether the alleged regulatory omissions present fit, concrete disputes ripe for review.

issues.label: Standard of review
issues.why: The court must apply the correct TSCA/APA standard (arbitrary and capricious/substantial evidence as applicable) to EPA’s choices.

issues.label: Chevron not applicable; statutory meaning
issues.why: The court must interpret §6(h)(4) and related provisions using current deference doctrines and traditional tools of construction.

issues.label: Administrative record scope
issues.why: The court must determine the proper record for review, including reconsideration materials and comments.

issues.label: Issue exhaustion
issues.why: The court must assess whether petitioners preserved arguments by raising them during notice-and-comment on reconsideration.

issues.label: Adequacy of notice-and-comment
issues.why: The court must decide whether EPA provided proper notice, opportunity to comment, and a logical outgrowth in the 2024 amendments.

issues.label: Reasoned explanation requirement
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether EPA adequately explained its regulatory choices and responses to significant comments.

issues.label: TSCA §6(h) applicability to decaBDE
issues.why: The court must confirm decaBDE meets §6(h)(1) criteria (toxic, high persistence/bioaccumulation, likely exposure) triggering expedited action.

issues.label: Deadline compliance relevance
issues.why: The court must consider whether EPA’s missed statutory proposal/final deadlines affect validity or remedy.

issues.label: Meaning of 'shall address risks'
issues.why: The court must interpret whether §6(h)(4) obligates EPA to regulate all identified risk pathways or permits selective action.

issues.label: Meaning of 'reduce exposure'
issues.why: The court must construe the breadth of the mandate to reduce exposure and how far it extends beyond direct manufacturing bans.

issues.label: Meaning of 'to the extent practicable'
issues.why: The court must define practicability (technical feasibility, cost, implementation constraints, enforceability) and its limits under §6(h)(4).

issues.label: Role of costs in §6(h)
issues.why: The court must decide how EPA may weigh compliance costs against exposure reduction given §6(h)’s text and structure.

issues.label: Policy goal of promoting recycling
issues.why: The court must determine whether EPA may treat recycling promotion as a permissible factor within §6(h)(4) practicability.

issues.label: Low-level exposure rationale
issues.why: The court must assess whether EPA’s finding of “low levels” of exposure is supported and legally sufficient to decline controls.

issues.label: Evidence supporting exposure findings
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether record evidence supports EPA’s exposure characterizations for recycling, disposal, wastewater, and sludge.

issues.label: Treatment of susceptible subpopulations
issues.why: The court must consider whether EPA adequately addressed higher-risk or susceptible groups as required by §6(h)(1).

issues.label: Lifecycle/conditions-of-use coverage
issues.why: The court must decide whether §6(h) requires comprehensive lifecycle regulation where exposure is likely at multiple stages.

issues.label: Regulation of recycling activities
issues.why: The court must decide whether limiting controls to one pallet recycler (PPE/signage) satisfies §6(h)(4) for plastics recycling generally.

issues.label: Adequacy of PPE-only measures
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether PPE/warnings are a practicable and sufficient exposure-reduction approach versus broader restrictions or bans.

issues.label: Articles and recycled-plastic products
issues.why: The court must decide how TSCA and EPA’s article definition affect authority/obligation to regulate articles containing decaBDE.

issues.label: Regulating manufacture of new articles
issues.why: The court must assess whether making new articles from recycled plastic (without adding new decaBDE) is within EPA’s required risk-addressing scope.

issues.label: Distribution-in-commerce limits
issues.why: The court must interpret the extent of EPA’s authority/obligation to restrict distribution of decaBDE-containing articles and recycled materials.

issues.label: Disposal regulation omission
issues.why: The court must decide whether §6(h)(4) requires EPA to regulate disposal pathways and, if not, whether EPA’s refusal is reasoned.

issues.label: Wastewater discharge coverage
issues.why: The court must assess whether restricting discharges only for non-article manufacture/processing/distribution unlawfully omits article-related discharges.

issues.label: Authority over article-related discharges
issues.why: The court must determine whether TSCA §6(h)/§6(a) authorizes controls on releases from facilities handling decaBDE-containing articles.

issues.label: Sewage sludge as fertilizer
issues.why: The court must decide whether EPA must address decaBDE in sludge land-application and whether EPA’s stated factor-based response is adequate.

issues.label: Air/soil release omissions
issues.why: The court must consider whether EPA unlawfully failed to address releases to air and soil associated with disputed lifecycle stages.

issues.label: Byproducts and breakdown products
issues.why: The court must consider whether risks from degradation into more persistent/toxic byproducts must be addressed in selecting controls.

issues.label: Interplay with RCRA
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether reliance on RCRA to decline TSCA controls is permissible or an unlawful abdication under §6(h)(4).

issues.label: Preemption/overlap principles
issues.why: The court must consider how TSCA interacts with other federal programs when EPA chooses not to regulate under TSCA due to other statutes.

issues.label: Bluewater staged regulation defense
issues.why: The court must decide whether and how Bluewater allows staged regulation under TSCA §6(h) given the mandatory exposure-reduction language.

issues.label: Limits on staged regulation
issues.why: The court must assess whether EPA identified a concrete plan/timeline for later regulation or impermissibly left risk unaddressed indefinitely.

issues.label: Rational connection to statutory factors
issues.why: The court must check that EPA’s reasons (cost, low exposure, recycling goals, other statutes) align with §6(h)(4) and record facts.

issues.label: Arbitrary-and-capricious omissions
issues.why: The court must determine whether EPA ignored important aspects of the problem, including significant exposure pathways petitioners identified.

issues.label: Consistency with prior findings
issues.why: The court must assess whether EPA’s “likely exposure at all stages” statements can be reconciled with declining to regulate major stages.

issues.label: Treatment of comments and evidence
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether EPA addressed significant comments from petitioners and experts about recycling, disposal, discharges, and sludge.

issues.label: Consideration of alternatives
issues.why: The court must decide whether EPA adequately considered less burdensome or different practicable measures (e.g., bans, limits, labeling, disposal standards).

issues.label: Enforceability and administrability
issues.why: The court must assess whether EPA reasonably evaluated whether broader recycling/disposal/sludge rules are enforceable and practicable.

issues.label: Definition and scope of 'practicable'
issues.why: The court must decide whether EPA applied an overly narrow view of practicability (e.g., treating high cost alone as dispositive).

issues.label: Regulated community identification
issues.why: The court must consider whether EPA improperly tailored controls to a single known recycler rather than the category of activities creating exposure.

issues.label: Equal treatment and arbitrary line-drawing
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether EPA drew rational distinctions between regulated and unregulated facilities/activities involving decaBDE.

issues.label: Adequacy of findings for exemptions
issues.why: The court must determine whether any exclusions (e.g., articles) are supported by findings consistent with §6(h)(4).

issues.label: Legal basis for partial prohibition
issues.why: The court must ensure EPA’s chosen mix of prohibitions/restrictions fits within §6(a) tools as incorporated by §6(h).

issues.label: Procedural regularity of reconsideration
issues.why: The court must decide whether EPA’s reconsideration process and final amendments complied with APA and TSCA procedural requirements.

issues.label: Remedy: vacatur vs remand
issues.why: The court must select the proper remedy and apply equitable factors for vacatur or remand without vacatur if errors are found.

issues.label: Remedy scope and instructions
issues.why: The court must decide whether it can order deadlines or specific rulemaking actions (180-day proposal, one-year final) and the limits on such relief.

issues.label: Severability of rule provisions
issues.why: The court must determine whether any unlawful provisions or omissions can be severed without upsetting the overall regulatory scheme.

issues.label: Harmless error doctrine
issues.why: The court must consider whether any procedural flaws were prejudicial or harmless under the APA.

issues.label: Amici positions relevance
issues.why: The court must consider arguments from amici (public health experts, iGPS Logistics) insofar as they bear on record, practicability, and impacts.
